tldr: This is not one story: the seven papers share only the phrase "case study" or "empirical study" in their titles. They form a loose November run of arXiv work that measures how agents and models actually behave, covering where long-horizon errors enter, what token spend tracks, KV cache reuse, benchmark throttling, web-element hallucination and over-editing coding agents.
whats_new: The newest paper finds that adding a generated helper image to visual question answering lowers mean accuracy by 3.7 points across 13 model pairs, with declines on nine of ten tasks.
why_it_matters: The common thread is measurement: several of these papers test whether a number teams already rely on (pass rate, token spend, benchmark score) means what they assume it means.

beats.headline: Two papers trace agent failures back to their origin
beats.summary: One follows long-horizon trajectories to where an error first enters. The other uses mechanistic interpretability on web agents that hallucinate page elements.

beats.headline: Token spend and benchmark scores are tested as proxies
beats.summary: One links five weeks of engineers' coding-agent token usage to their output. The other asks whether a model can be driven to a target score while looking like a naturally weaker model.

beats.headline: KV cache reuse across a model update, tested on DeepSeek-V4-Flash
beats.summary: An infrastructure outlier in the cluster: it asks what a cached prefix still preserves after the model weights change.

beats.headline: Coding agents' unneeded edits measured by revert-and-retest
beats.summary: Delta Residue Attribution reverts each patch unit and reruns the tests, across 7,660 Copilot CLI trajectories from 18 models. Any edit the tests do not need counts as over-editing.

beats.headline: A generated helper image lowers visual-reasoning accuracy by 3.7 points
beats.summary: Across 13 model pairs, adding a generated image to visual question answering hurt accuracy on nine of ten tasks.

open_questions: Does the over-edit study report which of the 18 models over-edit least, and by how much?
Does the token-spend paper find any correlation between spend and merged engineering output?
Does the DeepSeek-V4-Flash study find any cached state that survives a weight update without degrading outputs?
Does the long-horizon study name a control that catches errors at the step where they enter?
Does the image-generation study say what set apart the one task without a decline?
take_for_builders: If you gate coding-agent patches on passing tests alone, add a diff-size or revert-and-retest check, because a passing patch can still carry edits the tests never needed.
